# Testing {#sec-testing}

The layering from @sec-shape pays off here. Each layer can be tested on its own, most of them
without a window, and the tests run in seconds.

## Test each layer without the UI {#sec-test-layers}

| Layer | Test with | Needs a window |
|---|---|---|
| Core (plain C++) | any C++ test framework, such as Catch2 | no |
| View models and stores | Qt Test | no |
| QML components | Qt Quick Test | yes, offscreen |

A view model test calls commands and checks state and signals, exactly as the view would:

```{.cpp filename="tst_SketchbookViewModel.cpp"}
class tst_SketchbookViewModel : public QObject
{
    Q_OBJECT

private Q_SLOTS:
    void createAddsAnOpenSketch()
    {
        QTemporaryDir dir;                                       // <1>
        SketchStorage storage(dir.path());
        CanvasStore canvas;
        SketchbookViewModel viewModel(storage, canvas);
        QSignalSpy opened(&viewModel, &SketchbookViewModel::openNameChanged);  // <2>

        viewModel.create();

        QCOMPARE(viewModel.model()->rowCount(), 1);
        QCOMPARE(opened.count(), 1);
    }
};

QTEST_GUILESS_MAIN(tst_SketchbookViewModel)
#include "tst_SketchbookViewModel.moc"
```
1. A fresh folder per test: no test sees another test's files.
2. `QSignalSpy` records every emission of a signal.

::: {.more}
**Template:** `tests/sketchbook/`

**Read more:** [Qt Test overview](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtest-overview.html)
:::

## Test QML components {#sec-quick-test}

Qt Quick Test runs test cases written in QML. A test creates the component, simulates input,
and checks properties and signals:

```{.qml filename="tst_StrokeItem.qml"}
import QtQuick
import QtTest
import App.Canvas

TestCase {
    id: testCase
    name: "StrokeItem"
    width: 200
    height: 200
    visible: true
    when: windowShown

    Component {
        id: itemComponent
        StrokeItem { anchors.fill: parent }
    }

    SignalSpy {
        id: finished
        signalName: "strokeFinished"
    }

    function test_dragReportsThePoints(): void {
        const item = createTemporaryObject(itemComponent, testCase);
        finished.target = item;

        mousePress(item, 10, 10);
        mouseMove(item, 90, 80, -1, Qt.LeftButton);
        mouseRelease(item, 90, 80);

        compare(finished.count, 1);
    }
}
```

Setting `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` lets tests run without a screen, and the template sets
it in its test presets.

::: {.more}
**Template:** `tests/canvas/tst_StrokeItem.qml`

**Read more:** [Qt Quick Test](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtquicktest-index.html)
:::

## Tests must be deterministic {#sec-determinism}

A test that fails one run in twenty is worse than no test: people learn to ignore it.

- **Never sleep for a fixed time.** Wait for the condition instead: `QTRY_VERIFY` and
  `QTRY_COMPARE` in C++, `tryVerify()` and `tryCompare()` in QML.
- **Isolate state.** Use temporary directories instead of real paths, and simple test versions
  at the seams (@sec-interfaces) instead of the network or the clock.
- **No order dependence.** Each test sets up what it needs and cleans up after itself.

```cpp
QTest::qWait(500);                    // flaky: sometimes 500 ms is not enough
QTRY_COMPARE(spy.count(), 1);         // waits until true, or fails after a timeout
```

## Check your models {#sec-model-tester}

Item models have strict rules: row counts must match the signals, indexes must stay valid,
and every change needs the right begin and end calls. `QAbstractItemModelTester` checks all
of them while your test runs:

```cpp
SketchListModel model;
QAbstractItemModelTester tester(
    &model, QAbstractItemModelTester::FailureReportingMode::QtTest);
// every change to model is now verified
```

::: {.more}
**Read more:** [QAbstractItemModelTester](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qabstractitemmodeltester.html)
:::
